gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta spaces its tall-bodied letters far apart, every stroke cut like ribbon, against Groovy and its nearly shut c. Give the sans-serif body a little extra size.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-montserrat-alternat: Funky slit meets open paperclip curves. Groovy nearly closes its c, while Montserrat Alternates bends its own like a paperclip, so nudge the sans-serif body up a size.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-cascadia-code: Impact Label stands heavy, each letter a bead on a rod. Cascadia Code, a sans traced in one wire-like line, makes the weight gap the standout quality here.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-cascadia-mono: Impact Label hits hard with isolated, bead-like letters and a high x-height, its c ends flaring apart like pincers. One brings punch; Cascadia Mono, the sans-serif, brings compact, thickness-matched curves.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-julius-sans-o: Commanding and heavy, Impact Label sets each letter like a bead on a rod. Julius Sans One, a plain sans with vast gaps between letters, supplies the sharpest contrast.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-exa: Loud letters, every one standing alone. Impact Label does blunt, high-set display best, while Lexend Exa, a sans-serif, handles the quieter work with distinct curves and a large x-height.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-giga: Heavy hits, then widely spaced words. Impact Label excels at blunt headlines, while Lexend Giga, a sans-serif, lays down flat single-weight lines with ascenders barely clearing the x-height.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-mega: Impact Label is built for blunt force, each heavy letter standing apart with pincer-like c ends. And Lexend Mega, a sans-serif, handles the quieter work with one-nib lines and a visible gap in every c.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-tera: Lexend Tera draws plotter-pen lines with stepping-stone spacing, a thin foil against the heavy letters of Impact Label. One shouts from above, the other murmurs below in open-faced curves.
gen-dafont-impact-label-gf-lexend-zetta: Lexend Zetta cuts tall-bodied, widely tracked letters like ribbon, with zero stroke contrast. Lexend Zetta, a sans, can happily go a size up next to heavy Impact Label.
